existing_capabilities: resp2-parser (simple str, error, integer, bulk string, array; nested/limits)

missing_capabilities.name: auth-credential-spray
missing_capabilities.description: Module never attempts AUTH. Redis supports two forms: legacy 'AUTH password' (requirepass) and ACL 'AUTH user password' (Redis 6+, RESP2/3). recce should attempt a small default list against -NOAUTH endpoints ('', 'foobared', 'redis', 'password', 'admin', product/hostname derived) and consume creds from the credential store. Currently a locked instance is dead-ended as 'reachable but not a finding'.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Redis commands: AUTH (https://redis.io/commands/auth/); ACL AUTH form since 6.0

missing_capabilities.name: cve-2022-0543-lua-sandbox-escape
missing_capabilities.description: Debian/Ubuntu-packaged Redis leaves package.loadlib reachable from the Lua sandbox, giving unauth RCE via EVAL. A one-shot probe 'EVAL "if package and package.loadlib then return 1 else return 0 end" 0' cleanly distinguishes vulnerable builds. High-signal, actively exploited (Muhstik/Redigo botnets).

missing_capabilities.name: slaveof-replicaof-write-probe
missing_capabilities.description: Detect whether SLAVEOF/REPLICAOF is reachable — the redis-rogue-server / RedisModule-Load-over-replication chain (Pavel Toporkov, 2018) is the primary Redis-master-slave RCE. Sending 'REPLICAOF NO ONE' is a benign, reversible read-only probe: -NOPERM/renamed → hardened; +OK → the rogue-master RCE primitive is reachable. Currently the finding claims 'SLAVEOF ... role=master' by inference alone.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Redis REPLICAOF/SLAVEOF (https://redis.io/commands/replicaof/); Pavel Toporkov 'You got pwned by 6379'

missing_capabilities.name: cluster-nodes-topology
missing_capabilities.description: 'CLUSTER NODES' / 'CLUSTER SHARDS' returns full cluster peer list: node-id, ip:port, master/slave flags, slot ranges. Every peer is a new attack target (identical AUTH, same requirepass, often same modules). Currently uncalled — cluster deployments are enumerated as one host.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Redis Cluster spec §8 Command Overview: CLUSTER NODES/SHARDS (https://redis.io/docs/reference/cluster-spec/)

missing_capabilities.name: sentinel-port-and-commands
missing_capabilities.description: Redis Sentinel runs on TCP 26379 and answers a different command set: SENTINEL MASTERS / SENTINEL SLAVES <name> / SENTINEL SENTINELS <name> / SENTINEL CKQUORUM. Reveals monitored master ip/port, replica ip/port, peer sentinel addrs, and — critically — the 'auth-pass' field (replication password stored in cleartext in sentinel's view of a master). Port 26379 is not in _PORTS and no sentinel branch exists.

missing_capabilities.name: client-list-source-harvest
missing_capabilities.description: 'CLIENT LIST' returns id/addr/laddr/name/cmd for every connected client. addr= is a real internal IP:port using this Redis (feeds relay_targets/host graph); name= often includes the app identifier. Not called.

missing_capabilities.name: config-get-masterauth-and-secrets
missing_capabilities.description: 'CONFIG GET masterauth' returns the replication password in plaintext; 'CONFIG GET *' also leaks 'notify-keyspace-events', 'unixsocket', 'tls-cert-file', 'aclfile', 'user' directives. masterauth in particular is a real credential worth feeding into the hash/known_password store.

missing_capabilities.name: acl-getuser-and-user-enumeration
missing_capabilities.description: 'ACL LIST' is scanned but only for 'default nopass'. 'ACL USERS' returns every configured username; 'ACL GETUSER <name>' returns per-user passwords (hashed via SHA-256, feedable to hashcat -m 1400), enabled commands, key patterns, and channel ACLs. Currently discards every user beyond 'default' — a rich known_users + hash feed is left on the wire.

missing_capabilities.name: rename-command-hardening-detection
missing_capabilities.description: 'COMMAND COUNT' + 'COMMAND INFO' / 'COMMAND LIST' reveals whether CONFIG, FLUSHALL, SAVE, MODULE, DEBUG, SHUTDOWN, EVAL, SLAVEOF have been renamed or disabled via redis.conf rename-command. The finding currently claims all four RCE primitives are reachable when it may just be MODULE — differentiating hardened vs open sharpens severity and runbook.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Redis COMMAND / COMMAND INFO (https://redis.io/commands/command/); redis.conf rename-command

missing_capabilities.name: keyspace-scan-and-sample-loot
missing_capabilities.description: SCAN cursor + TYPE + (GET/HGETALL/LRANGE/SMEMBERS/JSON.GET) on a sample of keys — recce currently reports the key count but never samples. Cached session tokens, JWTs, Django/Flask session dicts (SESSION_*, sess:*), Sidekiq/Celery payloads with credentials, and RediSearch indexes are all standard finds. Runbook mentions it; module never does it. Cross-feeds hashes/known_users/tokens.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Redis SCAN (https://redis.io/commands/scan/); TYPE, GET, HGETALL, LRANGE, SMEMBERS

missing_capabilities.name: hello-resp3-and-tls-negotiation
missing_capabilities.description: 'HELLO' (Redis 6+) returns server version, mode, role, id, and — with 'HELLO 2 AUTH user pass' — supports auth in the handshake plus RESP3 downgrade signaling. Also useful to detect TLS-only listeners on 6380: recce's doc even lists 'ssl' as a return field but the code never populates it. No STARTTLS-style probe or ssl.wrap_socket fallback on 6380/16379.

missing_capabilities.name: module-fingerprint-and-known-cves
missing_capabilities.description: MODULE LIST returns module name+version but the module never maps them to known-vulnerable versions: RediSearch <2.6 (CVE-2023-31655), RedisGraph <2.10.3 (CVE-2023-31655/CVE-2022-24735 GRAPH.QUERY sandbox), RedisJSON path traversal, RedisBloom versions. Reported modules today feed only the string list.

missing_capabilities.name: cve-2023-41056-rdb-integer-overflow
missing_capabilities.description: Redis 7.0.x < 7.0.13 and 7.2.x < 7.2.1 have an integer overflow in string handling reachable by any authenticated user; combined with unauth this is a pre-auth crash/RCE. Version comparison currently only checks <6.0 EOL; the 7.x CVE band is silently ignored.

missing_capabilities.name: cve-2024-31449-lua-bit-library-bof
missing_capabilities.description: Redis < 7.2.5 / < 7.4.0 has a stack buffer overflow in the Lua bit library reachable via EVAL. Version-range check; not currently in _old_version()'s scope.

missing_capabilities.name: debug-command-availability
missing_capabilities.description: 'DEBUG SLEEP 0' / 'DEBUG OBJECT <key>' presence reveals whether DEBUG has been renamed. DEBUG SEGFAULT is a free DoS; DEBUG RELOAD forces RDB round-trip. A benign 'DEBUG SLEEP 0' probe classifies hardening.

missing_capabilities.name: pubsub-and-keyspace-notification-leak
missing_capabilities.description: 'CONFIG GET notify-keyspace-events' + 'PSUBSCRIBE __keyspace@*__:*' on an idle window reveals live app events (SET session:<id>, DEL token:*) — session hijack material in real time. Not attempted.

missing_capabilities.name: info-all-sections
missing_capabilities.description: Only default INFO is fetched (Server/Clients/Memory/Stats/Replication/CPU/Keyspace). 'INFO everything' adds commandstats (hot commands, telling app fingerprint), latencystats, and errorstats. Missed richer fingerprint context.

missing_capabilities.name: protected-mode-vs-bind-signal
missing_capabilities.description: CONFIG GET bind is not read. protected-mode-yes + bind 0.0.0.0 is the exact 'safe' misconfig where AUTH still isn't required from loopback — reading bind narrows the false-positive band on the unauth finding.

priority_gaps: cve-2022-0543-lua-sandbox-escape — one-shot EVAL probe, most-exploited Redis RCE in the wild, currently invisible
auth-credential-spray — no AUTH attempts at all; add small default list + credential-store consumption so locked instances become findings
acl-getuser-and-user-enumeration — leaks usernames + SHA-256 hashes hostile to hashcat -m 1400; direct known_users + hashes feed
cluster-nodes-topology + sentinel-port-26379 — cluster/sentinel peers currently invisible; feeds hosts/relay_targets and (via sentinel auth-pass) plaintext replication creds
cross_service_wire_gaps: known_users: ACL USERS and ACL GETUSER output (usernames + per-user allowed commands/keys) — currently discarded past 'default nopass' scan
hashes: ACL GETUSER returns per-user SHA-256 password hashes (hashcat -m 1400) — never harvested
hashes/known_passwords: CONFIG GET masterauth returns replication password in plaintext — never fetched
hashes/known_passwords: SENTINEL MASTER <name> exposes monitored master's auth-pass in plaintext — sentinel branch missing entirely
relay_targets/hosts: CLUSTER NODES / CLUSTER SHARDS output enumerates every cluster peer ip:port — never fetched
relay_targets/hosts: CLIENT LIST addr= gives internal IPs of every app currently talking to this Redis — never fetched
hosts: INFO replication slaveN=ip=...,port=... lines are only summarised (connected_slaves count) — individual replica IPs discarded
loot/known_secrets: SCAN + GET/HGETALL of session:*, token:*, jwt:*, cred:* keys yields live session tokens and API keys — module never samples the keyspace it counts
service-catalog: MODULE LIST names (RediSearch, RedisGraph, RedisJSON, RedisBloom) should route to module-specific CVE checks and query surfaces
summary: recce/services/db/redis.py handles the unauth-INFO case with a clean stdlib RESP2 parser and the ACL/MODULE/replication side-signals, but the entire attack surface beyond 'is INFO answering?' is untouched: no AUTH attempts (credential spray, credential-store integration), no keyspace sampling (SCAN + GET/HGETALL for session/token loot), no Lua-sandbox CVE probe (CVE-2022-0543 — the most-exploited Redis RCE), no rogue-master replication probe, no Cluster/Sentinel enumeration (Sentinel port 26379 isn't even in _PORTS), no CLIENT LIST peer harvest, no ACL USERS/GETUSER user+hash extraction, no CONFIG masterauth pull, no rename-command hardening check, no TLS handshake on 6380 despite the docstring promising an 'ssl' field, and version-band CVEs after 6.0 (CVE-2023-41056, CVE-2024-31449) are ignored by _old_version. The highest-ROI additions are the CVE-2022-0543 probe, an AUTH default-cred spray, ACL user/hash enumeration, and Cluster+Sentinel topology (all four also close cross-service wire gaps into known_users/hashes/hosts/relay_targets that no other module can supply).
notes: Sentinel port 26379 is not in _PORTS — is_redis() misses sentinel entirely; SENTINEL command family and Sentinel auth-pass leak are downstream of that gap. The docstring in probe() lists 'ssl' as a returned key but the code never sets it — either drop the promise or add ssl.wrap_socket fallback on 6380/16379. _old_version()'s [6,0] cutoff is EOL-only and ignores post-6.0 CVEs; consider replacing with a per-CVE version-range matcher (CVE-2022-0543 hits all Debian-packaged versions regardless of upstream fix, so a Debian/Ubuntu 'os' hint from INFO would sharpen it). REPLICAOF NO ONE is safe to send against an already-master and is the canonical hardening probe for the SLAVEOF branch — the finding currently asserts SLAVEOF-reachable purely on role=master, which is a false positive whenever slaveof/replicaof has been renamed.
